sentences.text:
Author: Parth Prateem Sahu
Bench: Parth Prateem Sahu
1  NAFR  HIGH COURT OF CHHATTISGARH, BILASPUR  MCRC No. 702 of 2024   Rohit Ahirwar S/o Nanulal Ahirwar Aged About 20 Years R/o Village
Ramdi, Tehsil Kala Pipal, District Sajapur (M.P.)
(Wrongly Mentioned  As C.G. In The Impugned Order).
---- Applicant  Versus   State Of Chhattisgarh Through Police Station - Sarkanda District -  Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh).
---- Non-Applicant
For Applicant : Mr. Om Kukreja, Advocate
For State : Ms. Nandkumari Kashyap, Panel Lawyer  Hon'ble Shri Justice Parth Prateem Sahu  Order On Board 15/01/2024 1.

Applicant has filed this first bail application under Section 439 of CrPC for grant of regular bail as he was arrested in connection with Crime No. 1431 of 2023 registered at Police Station Sarkanda,
District - Bilaspur (C.G.) for offence punishable under Section 363, 366, 376 (2)(n) of I.P.C. &
Section 4 & 6 of POCSO Act.

2. Case of the prosecution is that, father of victim lodged report to the concerned Police Station on 25.10.2023 stating that on 24.10.2023, his daughter left the house at about 12:00 pm and thereafter did not returned back.
Based on the report, Initially, crime was registered against unknown person under Section 363 of I.P.C..
During investigation victim was recovered, her statement was recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., other offences were also added against applicant and he was arrested on 10.12.2023.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is innocent, he has not committed any offence of any nature as alleged.
Victim herself came to the village of applicant.
False allegations are levelled in the statement of victim recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C..
He contended that victim has not made any allegation of establishing physical relation with her in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C..
Applicant is a boy of tender age of 20 years and is in jail since 10.12.2023, hence, he may be enlarged on bail.

4. Learned State counsel opposes the submission made by learned counsel for applicant and submits that serious allegation of establishing physical relation is levelled by victim who is less than 18 years of age, in her statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.

However, upon putting specific query with regard to the statement of victim under Section 164, she did not dispute the submission of learned counsel for applicant based on the statement of victim recorded under Section 164.
5.
Pursuant to notice issued, father of victim appeared before this Court in person and submits that he is having no objection in grant of bail to the applicant.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also perused the documents enclosed with bail application.

7. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegation,
submission made by learned counsel for the applicant based upon the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. which is not opposed by learned State counsel, without commenting anything on merits of the case, I am inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail.
8. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on regular bail, upon furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court on the conditions that - a) Applicant shall appear before the Trial Court regularly on each and every date,
unless exempted from appearance.
b) The applicant shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c) If the applicant is found involved in similar offence in future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of Bail.
Certified copy as per rules.

Sd/-
 (Parth Prateem Sahu)
